answer: The admission kernel for a market trading lagoon surveys and juniper crop data accepts one vote per certified secure chip. A chip signs the epoch beacon and agent key using its non-exportable factory key. Validators verify the certificate and signature, then reject duplicate chip identifiers or stale epochs. Resetting software cannot change that identifier. Each extra alias therefore needs another purchased chip, and parallel registration still consumes one chip per seat. Security depends on honest certificate issuance and resistance to key extraction; rented chips remain a cost.
